app_info.subtitle: Operate your paired computers
app_info.description: ReMCP lets an authenticated user securely operate computers they explicitly paired: native desktop UI through Accessibility/UI Automation, debuggable Chromium pages through loopback DOM/CDP, keyboard/pointer input, files and terminal sessions, services/logs/network diagnostics, screenshots, and structured PDF/DOCX/XLSX operations. Every device has its own revocable credential and connects outbound, so no inbound port is opened. Semantic UI and browser DOM are preferred before OCR or coordinates. Every tool carries explicit read-only, destructive, idempotent, and open-world annotations matching its actual behavior. Reviewers can evaluate the surface against an isolated hosted sandbox that never touches a real computer.
app_info.release_notes:
# ReMCP 0.2.146 — release notes

Submission status: Initial public catalog submission. Previous submitted version: none.
Plugin version: 0.2.146
MCP endpoint: https://remcp.site/mcp
Tool count: 10

## What ReMCP does

ReMCP lets an authenticated user securely operate computers they explicitly paired. It provides semantic desktop control through Accessibility/UI Automation, browser DOM/CDP automation, keyboard/pointer input, files and terminal sessions, services/logs/network diagnostics, screenshots, and structured PDF/DOCX/XLSX operations while keeping every device behind an outbound, revocable agent connection.

## Reviewer setup

- Reviewer OAuth credentials are supplied only in the OpenAI submission portal; no credential or recovery material is stored in this repository.
- Positive case 1 exercises the reviewer account fleet with `list_devices`; no paired computer is required and the hosted `review-sandbox` must not appear in that list.
- Positive cases 2–5 use the fixed device id `review-sandbox`. It is a hosted synthetic fixture that never reaches a real paired computer.
- The sandbox seeds `/workspace/README.txt`, permits the exact-content `write_file` review case, and returns a clearly labelled synthetic screenshot PNG so native MCP text and image results can be reviewed without exposing private screen data.
- The five positive and three negative test cases are generated in `chatgpt-app-submission.json` and are designed to run without private-network access or additional setup.

## What changed

**OpenAI submission artifacts now carry the Apps-form fields that the live portal actually requires.**

- `chatgpt-app-submission.json` now includes the same reviewer-accessible demo recording URL as the Plugin Directory package plus the exact generated release notes for the current version.
- The submission generator and release preparation share one demo URL constant so Apps-form and ZIP metadata cannot drift.
- Live portal verification confirmed `DEVELOPER_TOOLS` persists correctly; the blocking field was the missing demo recording URL, while reviewer credentials remain intentionally portal-only and are never committed.
- Regression coverage fails if the legacy Apps JSON loses the demo URL or release notes, while the five positive / three negative reviewer cases and compact 10-tool hosted MCP contract remain unchanged.
- Runtime tool names, schemas, annotations, dynamic capability behavior, and the 83-operation local runtime surface are unchanged.

justifications.read_only_justification: Read only: it reads the account device list and relay connection state and returns the result without writing anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: Not open world: no external service is contacted.
justifications.destructive_justification: Not destructive: returns a list; nothing is created, changed or removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read only: it routes one signed-in ReMCP account operation: profile, recent calls, usage, hosted configuration, pairing creation, ping, rename, enable/disable, or permanent pairing removal, which changes state on the selected computer or in a running session.
justifications.open_world_justification: Not open world: account reads and writes stay inside ReMCP; ping reaches only the explicitly paired computer through the ReMCP relay.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the façade is conservatively destructive because operation=remove permanently revokes a pairing; inspection, ping, pairing creation, rename, and enable/disable are narrower operations validated separately.

justifications.read_only_justification: Read only: it reads a text file from the paired computer and returns the result without writing anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: Not open world: reads a local file only and never fetches URLs.
justifications.destructive_justification: Not destructive: returns file content without writing anything.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read only: it routes one explicitly selected filesystem operation on the paired computer, including reads, edits, search, archives, copies, moves, permissions, or deletion, which changes state on the selected computer or in a running session.
justifications.open_world_justification: Not open world: filesystem operations are local to the selected paired computer and do not fetch URLs.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the façade is conservatively destructive because contained operations can overwrite, move, permission-change, or permanently delete local paths; the concrete operation retains its original closed schema and policy.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read only: it routes one explicitly selected terminal-session operation on the paired computer, including starting commands, reading or waiting for output, interaction, termination, or session listing, which changes state on the selected computer or in a running session.
justifications.open_world_justification: Open world: a started or interactive command can contact external services with the rights of the local agent account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the façade is conservatively destructive because command execution, process input, and termination can change state or lose unsaved work; read-only terminal operations remain narrower at dispatch.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read only: it routes one explicitly selected native desktop operation, including semantic inspection of windows/accessibility/displays or actions such as window/app control, text/keyboard/pointer input, clipboard, path opening, notifications, or bounded recording, which changes state on the selected computer or in a running session.
justifications.open_world_justification: Open world: the controlled local application can itself communicate with external services, so some contained action operations can have open-world effects.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the façade is conservatively destructive because contained operations can change application state, enter or submit data, close windows, replace clipboard content, or create a recording; inspection operations remain read-only at dispatch.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read only: it routes one pixel-producing operation: read a local image, capture the desktop, or capture a selected window/monitor/region, which changes state on the selected computer or in a running session.
justifications.open_world_justification: Not open world: image reads and captures use local files or local screen facilities only.
justifications.destructive_justification: Not destructive: returns image content; screenshot operations may create only their explicitly requested bounded local capture artifact and do not overwrite unrelated user data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read only: it routes one explicitly selected loopback Chrome DevTools Protocol operation for tabs, navigation, DOM/accessibility inspection, element actions, waits, or JavaScript evaluation, which changes state on the selected computer or in a running session.
justifications.open_world_justification: Open world: the controlled browser page may access internet or intranet services, navigate, submit requests, or execute page JavaScript.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the façade is conservatively destructive because contained actions can submit forms, upload files, navigate, or change remote website data; inspection operations remain read-only at dispatch.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read only: it routes one explicitly selected operating-system or ReMCP runtime operation for system/process facts, preferences, services, logs, networking, installed apps, environment, audio, or power, which changes state on the selected computer or in a running session.
justifications.open_world_justification: Open world: some contained operations can contact a requested network host or affect a service that communicates externally.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the façade is conservatively destructive because it includes process termination, service changes, runtime preference changes, audio changes, and power actions; read-only diagnostics remain narrower at dispatch.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read only: it routes one explicitly selected structured document operation for reading supported documents or editing XLSX, DOCX, and PDF files, which changes state on the selected computer or in a running session.
justifications.open_world_justification: Not open world: operates only on permitted local document paths and does not fetch URLs.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the façade is conservatively destructive because editing operations can replace local document content or output files; read_document remains read-only at dispatch.

test_cases.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account; no paired computer is required. List the account computers and verify the hosted review fixture is not exposed as a real device.
test_cases.user_prompt: List my ReMCP devices and tell me which ones are online.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a device list with user-facing machine identity and online state; an empty real-device list is valid. The fixed review-sandbox fixture is intentionally absent.

test_cases.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account and fixed device id review-sandbox. Its seeded workspace contains README.txt. Browse the sandbox workspace without changing it.
test_cases.user_prompt: Using ReMCP device id review-sandbox, list the files in /workspace.
test_cases.expected_output: Calls manage_files with operation=list_directory and returns the sandbox directory entries, including the seeded README fixture, without modifying the workspace.

test_cases.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account and fixed device id review-sandbox with the seeded README.txt fixture. Read and summarize the seeded text file.
test_cases.user_prompt: Using ReMCP device id review-sandbox, read /workspace/README.txt and summarize it.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the seeded review README as text so ChatGPT can summarize it; no real computer data is read.

test_cases.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account and fixed device id review-sandbox. Its screenshot action returns a labelled synthetic PNG as native MCP image content.
test_cases.user_prompt: Using ReMCP device id review-sandbox, take a screenshot and show it.
test_cases.expected_output: Calls view_image with operation=take_screenshot and returns the labelled synthetic Review Sandbox PNG as native MCP image content for model vision plus a short-lived preview reference when custom widgets are enabled; no real screen capture is involved.

test_cases.description: Fixture: use the dedicated reviewer OAuth account and fixed device id review-sandbox with its writable sandbox workspace. Exercise the exact-content write case.
test_cases.user_prompt: Using ReMCP device id review-sandbox, create /workspace/review-note.txt containing exactly: ReMCP submission test.
test_cases.expected_output: Calls manage_files with operation=write_file, creates or replaces only the requested sandbox review note with the exact text, and returns the write result. No real computer is modified.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke ReMCP for general weather information.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What will the weather be in Warsaw tomorrow?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: ReMCP should not be invoked because the request does not involve a paired computer.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke ReMCP for standalone writing help.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Draft a polite email asking my landlord to repair a leaking faucet.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: ReMCP should not be invoked because no local computer action or data is needed.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke ReMCP for a conceptual technical explanation.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Explain OAuth PKCE in simple terms.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: ReMCP should not be invoked because the user only requested an explanation.
